headline: Q2 METALS DRILLS BEST HOLE IN COMPANY HISTORY: 403.7m AT 1.57% Li₂O AT CISCO LITHIUM, QUEBEC — SECOND INTERCEPT HITS 213.8m AT 1.93% Li₂O
snippet: Q2 Metals Corp. (TSX-V: QTWO) reported August 25 that Hole 93 at its Cisco Lithium Project in Quebec's James Bay region is the best hole drilled in company history: a 213.8-metre intercept at 1.93% Li₂O followed by a 403.7-metre intercept at 1.57% Li₂O, with a near-surface hit of 60.8 metres at 1.24% Li₂O starting only 14 metres from surface. The 403.7-metre interval demonstrates continuity of the western deposit at depth, with approximately 170 metres occurring outside the April 2026 Mineral Resource Estimate pit shell — meaning this depth extension directly adds to the resource inventory. At spodumene concentrate above $2,000/tonne and lithium carbonate up 94.56% year-over-year, a 403-metre intercept at 1.57% Li₂O from a Canadian tier-one jurisdiction is the exact result that unlocks pre-feasibility financing conversations: it proves that the western extension of Cisco has both the grade and the scale to support an open-pit mine development.

headline: SARFARTOQ ECONOMIC BOMB: $2.05B NPV, 118.6% PRE-TAX IRR FOR GREENLAND'S 40,700t NdPr DEPOSIT — FIRST ECONOMIC STUDY ON WEST'S KEY MAGNET RARE EARTH PROJECT
snippet: Greenland Mines Ltd. (NASDAQ: GRML) released an independent Initial Assessment on August 25 for the Sarfartoq Nd-Pr Rare Earth Project in southwest Greenland, confirming a high-case pre-tax NPV (8% real) of US$2.05 billion and an IRR of 118.6% including both Indicated and Inferred mineral resources — and US$1.49 billion NPV at 92.7% IRR on Indicated resources only. The study was prepared by Tetra Tech Canada and GeoSim Services and is the first economic analysis of the project's 40,700 tonnes of contained NdPr oxide, equivalent to roughly five years of all NdPr refined outside China in 2025. The 118.6% IRR at current rare earth prices — before factoring in any U.S. government offtake premium or defense procurement preference under Executive Order 14415 — indicates the project is viable without subsidies and competitive with the best-returning development assets in any critical mineral category. The announcement follows yesterday's maiden Indicated resource and is the clearest signal yet that Sarfartoq is moving from exploration to development decision at the moment allied nations most urgently need non-Chinese NdPr supply.

headline: ANDINA COPPER INTERSECTS 206m AT 0.67% CU FROM 32m — COBRASCO PORPHYRY IN COLOMBIA EXTENDS HIGHER-GRADE CORE TO 276m WITHIN 400m AT 0.46% CU
snippet: Andina Copper Corp. (TSX-V: ANDC) announced August 25 that Hole CDH011 at the Cobrasco porphyry copper-molybdenum discovery in Chocó, Colombia, returned 206 metres at 0.67% Cu from 32 metres depth within a broader 400-metre interval at 0.46% Cu, with the higher-grade upper zone extending to 276 metres downhole and moderate-grade Cu-Mo mineralization continuing to approximately 592 metres. CDH011 confirms vertical continuity of mineralization within the central portion of the Cobrasco system at shallow, near-surface depths that support open-pit mine economics. Colombia's Chocó is an underexplored Andean porphyry corridor; at copper above $14,000/tonne, a 206-metre intercept starting 32 metres from surface in a porphyry system with confirmed molybdenum byproduct revenue is the combination of attributes that attracts major producer interest: shallow geometry, wide mineralized system, and a commodity in structural deficit for multiple years.

headline: SOUTHERN CROSS GOLD DRILLS 1,466 g/t GOLD AT 886m DEPTH — RISING SUN EXTENDS DOWN-DIP TO 1,032m AT SUNDAY CREEK, VICTORIA
snippet: Southern Cross Gold Consolidated (TSX: SXGC / ASX: SX2) announced August 25 that Hole SDDSC230 at the Sunday Creek Gold-Antimony Project in Victoria, Australia, intersected 0.3 metres at 1,466.7 g/t AuEq (1,466.4 g/t Au, 0.1% Sb) from 886.7 metres — the 12th-best composite at the project — with an individual assay of 0.1 metres at 4,500 g/t Au, the fourth-highest single gold assay returned at Sunday Creek. The intersection represents a 166-metre down-dip extension from the prior high-grade intercept in SDDSC144, confirming vein-set RS19 at depth with unusually consistent grade: two high-grade intersections 166 metres apart in the same vein set is a strong indicator of plunge continuity, the geological attribute that supports large total resource inventories in structurally-controlled gold systems. Mineralization has now been identified to 1,031.7 metres depth. Victoria's Sunday Creek — a gold-antimony system in a tier-one Australian mining jurisdiction — has accumulated an updated exploration target of 3–4.6 million ounces; grade continuity at over 1,000 metres depth is the defining characteristic of a world-class orogenic gold discovery.

headline: DENARIUS METALS RETURNS 33m AT 5.68 g/t GOLD AT ZANCUDO — SANTA CATALINA STRUCTURE DELIVERS CONTINUOUS HIGH-GRADE IN COLOMBIA WHILE PROCESSING PLANT UNDER CONSTRUCTION
snippet: Denarius Metals Corp. (Cboe CA: DMET / OTCQX: DNRSF) reported August 25 that drill hole ZM-210 at the Las Brisas Target within the Zancudo Project in Colombia returned a 33-metre continuous interval grading 5.68 g/t Au on the Santa Catalina structure, including a high-grade core of 20.18 g/t Au over 3.1 metres. Zancudo is an operating mine in early production phase; Denarius is simultaneously drilling a 15,100-metre program for resource modelling and mine planning while constructing a 1,000-tonnes-per-day flotation processing plant expected to commence operations in 2026. For TSX-V investors, 5.68 g/t over 33 metres at a project already in production — rather than pre-discovery exploration — is the highest-confidence type of resource expansion drill result: it confirms that the mine footprint is growing while commercial production is already generating revenue, a combination that derisk both the geological model and the path to full-scale production.

headline: FURY GOLD RETURNS 14.41 g/t OVER 3.92m IN EAU CLAIRE INFILL — PHASE 2 DRILLING CONVERTS INFERRED TO INDICATED ACROSS JAMES BAY GOLD CORRIDOR
snippet: Fury Gold Mines Limited (TSX: FURY / NYSE American: FURY) released the third batch of assay results from its Phase 2 drill program at the Eau Claire Gold Project in Eeyou Istchee James Bay, Quebec on August 25, with standout results including 14.41 g/t gold over 3.92 metres. The Phase 2 program — 15,000 to 25,000 metres designed to upgrade inferred mineral resources to indicated — is targeting conversion of the resource ahead of a resource update expected later in 2026. Eau Claire sits within the James Bay gold corridor, one of Canada's most active exploration districts, where Cree Nation partnership frameworks and Quebec's established permitting environment reduce development risk. High-grade infill results like 14.41 g/t confirm the existing resource model holds at grade and provide confidence in the block model assumptions that underpin future economic studies — the foundational step before a preliminary economic assessment. At $4,637 gold and a Quebec project with established Indigenous partnerships, Eau Claire's resource upgrade pathway is direct and de-risked relative to projects in less stable jurisdictions.

headline: F3 URANIUM'S 950m TETRA STEPOUT RETURNS BLEACHING IDENTICAL TO DISCOVERY ZONE — PATTERN THAT PRECEDED THE ZONE'S ORIGINAL HIT AT ATHABASCA BASIN
snippet: F3 Uranium Corp. (TSX-V: FUU) reported August 25 that Hole PLN26-229 — a 950-metre step-out east of the Tetra Zone discovery on the Patterson Lake North Project in Saskatchewan's Western Athabasca Basin — intersected strong bleaching at the top of the basement comparable to the alteration signature seen at the Tetra Zone itself. A second hole, PLN26-228, tested the A4 conductor parallel to the A1 conductor that hosts the JR Zone 4 km to the southwest. The Tetra Zone is one of the Western Athabasca Basin's most significant recent uranium discoveries; finding the same bleaching pattern 950 metres away from the known zone in the first summer holes after discovery drilling confirms the alteration footprint is larger than the initial discovery zone. In Athabasca Basin uranium exploration, basement alteration of this type is the direct precursor to uranium mineralization — it indicates fluids capable of depositing uranium have moved through the system. For TSX-V uranium investors, a 950-metre stepout confirming the alteration halo is the geological setup that precedes resource-scale discoveries.

headline: NIGER NATIONALIZES FRANCE'S LAST SAHEL URANIUM MINE — ORANO'S SOMAÏR OPERATION TRANSFERRED TO STATE COMPANY TSUMCO SA
snippet: Niger's military government awarded a large-scale uranium mining permit previously held by French nuclear company Orano SA to a state-controlled entity called Tsumco SA — a company Niger created after nationalizing the Somaïr mine, France's last remaining uranium operation in the Sahel. The announcement, dated August 22, removes the final Western-operated uranium asset from the Sahel region following Niger's 2023 coup and subsequent expulsion of French military forces. France sourced approximately 25% of its nuclear fuel cycle's uranium requirements from Niger historically; the Somaïr transfer closes that supply channel permanently and forces French utility EDF to rely more heavily on Kazakhstan, Canada, and Uzbekistan for yellowcake supply. For uranium spot markets, the loss of Somaïr output — roughly 2,000 tonnes of U3O8 per year — compounds the structural supply shortfall already created by Kazatomprom's 10% guidance cut and Cameco's McArthur River reduction, tightening the 2027 utility contracting outlook for a fuel cycle already in deficit.

headline: DOE COMMITS $500M FOR SEVEN CRITICAL MINERAL PROJECTS — BATTERY PROCESSING, RECYCLING AND MANUFACTURING CHAINS GET LANDMARK FEDERAL BACKING
snippet: The U.S. Department of Energy's Office of Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation announced $500 million for seven selected projects targeting expansion of domestic critical mineral and material processing, battery manufacturing and recycling capacity. The awards focus on middle and downstream stages of the battery supply chain — where raw materials are refined into battery-grade products fed into cell manufacturing — and form part of the administration's broader effort to reduce dependence on Chinese-origin critical minerals and components ahead of the January 1, 2027 defence procurement restriction under Executive Order 14415. For TSX-V and ASX junior critical mineral developers with projects targeting lithium, cobalt, graphite, nickel, and rare earth processing, the DOE's $500M deployment is a direct upstream signal: it funds the processing infrastructure that defines which upstream projects have a credible path to a U.S. offtake buyer. Projects that can supply the battery-grade specifications required by DOE-backed processing facilities gain a decisive advantage in accessing North American financing chains.

headline: GOLD HOLDS $4,648 ON FISCAL RISK BID AS SILVER SLIPS — U.S. RECORD DEBT AND DOLLAR SLIDE SUSTAIN PRECIOUS METALS BULL MARKET THROUGH PROFIT-TAKING
snippet: Gold held near $4,648 per ounce in late-afternoon North American trading on August 24 while silver slipped modestly to $68.75 — with the divergence reflecting profit-taking in silver after its extraordinary August surge while gold's 'fiscal risk bid' held firm on U.S. debt concerns and a weakening dollar. Silver bulls' next technical target is $70.02; a break above that level opens $71.56 and then $72.08. The underlying bid is structural: U.S. government debt has crossed a new record, the Treasury's bond buyback program continues to compress long yields, and the dollar index remains weak against a basket of commodities currencies. For junior mining investors, the gold/silver divergence on August 24 — gold firm, silver profit-taking — reflects the typical pattern within a sustained bull market: the more liquid commodity (gold) holds while the smaller market (silver) shakes out weak longs before the next leg. Both metals remain at historically elevated levels relative to mining production costs, supporting continued sector outperformance.
